newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ market brushes off Medfly news to end weaker.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ market brushes off Medfly news to end weaker.

text.p: Not even a news of an emergency outbreak of the Mediterranean fruit fly in Florida could lift the FCOJ futures market out its torpor, as prices closed lower on the day.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman today declared an emergency outbreak of the Mediterranean fruit fly, one of the most destructive pests for citrus.
But with the 1996/97 harvest nearly complete, players said the pests are not likely to affect the crop, which has been estimated at a record 224.2 million 90-lb boxes.

Trade remained rangebound as players squared positions ahead of the first notice day for the July contract, on July 1. The market is likely to resume its downward trend once the contract goes off the board, dealers said.
Firm support in July was pegged at 70.00 cents.

The spot July contract settled 0.45 cent lower at 73.20 cents per lb, traded 74.00 to 72.90 cents. The most-active September contract ended down 0.45 cent at 76.05 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.15 cent weaker.
Traders said market activity will focus on the liquidation of the spot month ahead of first notice day on July 1. Open interest in July stood at 8,912 lots, down 1,908 lots, as of Wednesday.
An estimated 6,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Wednesday's official 5,774 lots.
Weekly movement, released after today's close, rose to 4.798 million gallons, compared with 4.146 million gallons the previous week.
